topic: Raymond Agentic Workflow: Let Agents Do Agent Work

key_points: The coordination problem is the biggest bottleneck in production multi-agent systems in 2026
Six coordination patterns: Fan-Out/Fan-In, Pipeline, Hierarchical Delegation, Blackboard, Handoff Chain
Covers CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen/AG2, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Claude Code
Agents should communicate through structured data, not freeform conversation
Each agent owns one outcome; orchestrator is thin and only plans/delegates
Four multi-agent patterns: Orchestrator-Worker, Handoff, Blackboard, Autonomous Swarm
Orchestrator-worker is the most-used pattern; orchestrator's only tools are the other agents
Structured handoff objects (summary + data + confidence + needs_review) beat string passing
Start with one agent; split only when it struggles (loses context, wrong tools, too slow)
Cost is 2-3x higher but accuracy improves (70% -> 90% on complex tasks in case study)
Anthropic's Dec 2024 taxonomy: chain, router, parallel, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
Andrew Ng showed GPT-3.5 with iterative workflow hit 95.1% HumanEval vs 67% GPT-4 zero-shot
Workflow choice determines latency, cost, reliability — not just architecture
Human-in-the-loop at three positions: pre-execution, post-execution blocking, by-exception
Start with simplest solution; only increase complexity when necessary
Shift from conductor (one agent, real-time) to orchestrator (ensemble, async coordination)
Three-tier model: in-process agents, local orchestrators, cloud async
Architect-Executor-Reviewer loop is the most common coordination pattern
Ralph Loop: stateless-but-iterative Pick->Implement->Validate->Commit->Reset
Worktree isolation prevents merge conflicts in parallel agent work
Workflows = predefined code paths; Agents = model dynamically decides steps
Understand when each strategy is appropriate

angles: Letting agents do agent work means moving from prompting one model to orchestrating a team of specialized workers
The core shift: from single-agent autonomy to multi-agent collaboration with clear division of labor
The coordination problem is the real bottleneck — not model capability
Design principle: each agent owns one outcome; orchestrators plan and delegate, they don't do the work
Start with one agent, then split along natural fault lines (context, tools, domain) — don't design multi-agent upfront
Communication is data, not conversation: structured handoffs beat freeform chat
Human-on-the-loop governance is the production default, not full autonomy
